title: Header parsing — Email Archive Extractor
description: Headers (From, To, Date, Subject) parse per RFC 5322 with folding and encoded words. The email package handles the edge cases. Headers frame the message.
demo:
# Email extraction: parse RFC822 messages (stdlib email), list headers + attachments + thread refs.
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
raw = """From: amy@x.test\nTo: bob@x.test\nDate: Mon, 1 Jan 2024 10:00:00 +0000\nSubject: Hello\nMessage-ID: <m1@x>\n\nHi Bob.""".replace("\\n", "\n").encode()
msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(raw)
print("From:", msg["from"], "| To:", msg["to"], "| Date:", msg["date"])
print("Subject:", msg["subject"])
print("Message-ID:", msg["message-id"], "| In-Reply-To:", msg["in-reply-to"])
n_att = 0
for part in msg.walk():
    if part.get_content_disposition() == "attachment":
        n_att += 1
        print(f"attachment: {part.get_filename()} ({len(part.get_payload(decode=True) or b'')} bytes)")
body = msg.get_body(preferencelist=("plain",))
print("body preview:", (body.get_content()[:60].replace("\n", " ") if body else "none"))
print("attachments:", n_att)
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.
